questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to design a modular, runtime-configurable data pipeline with per-tenant customization.

## Key Concepts
- Plugin architecture and the Pipeline pattern
- Immutable pipelines and copy-on-write config
- Per-tenant routing and hot-reload
- Stateless transforms and fault tolerance

## Code Example
```javascript
class Transform { constructor(name){this.name=name} apply(rec){return rec}}
class NormalizeTransform extends Transform { apply(r){ /* normalize */ return r} }
class Pipeline { constructor(steps){ this.steps=Object.freeze(steps)} process(r){ return this.steps.reduce((acc,t)=>t.apply(acc), r) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test per-tenant hot reload without downtime?
- How do you handle a failing plugin without aborting the whole record?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question probes designing a scalable, extensible command-dispatch system with runtime pluggability, ordering guarantees, and per-handler policies.

## Key Concepts
- Command Pattern and Mediator
- Runtime registries and type-safe dispatch
- Per-type queuing, concurrency, backpressure
- Policy hooks (retry, concurrency) and isolation

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { type: string; payload: any }
interface ICommandHandler { handle(cmd: Command): Promise<any> }
interface IPolicy { apply(context: any): void }
class Registry { register(type: string, h: ICommandHandler) { /* ... */ } lookup(type: string): ICommandHandler | undefined { /* ... */ } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you detect and prevent circular registrations?
- How would you test order guarantees under load?
- What are trade-offs vs a pure Mediator vs Event-driven approach?
